title: Loop-Powered Mini Game
summary: Build a mini game that uses loops, variables, and decisions together — your most powerful program yet.

content.title: What You Know Now
content.summary: You now have variables, `input`, `if`/`else`/`elif`, and `for` loops — enough to build a real game.
content.body:
Look at everything you can do:

• Variables — store and change information
• `input()` — ask the player questions
• `if` / `elif` / `else` — make decisions
• `for` loops — repeat actions automatically
• `range()` — control exactly how many times

That is enough to build a real interactive game.

content.title: The Project: Dungeon Run
content.summary: Ask for the hero's name, loop through rooms, make decisions in each room, end with a score.
content.body:
You will build a dungeon run game:

1. Ask the player for their hero's name
2. Loop through 5 rooms
3. In each room, something happens (safe, trap, treasure, or boss)
4. After the loop, print a victory message with their name

Here is a starting shape:
content.codeBlock:
name = input("Hero name? ")
for i in range(1, 6):
    print("Room", i, "...")
print(name, "wins!")

content.title: Making It Interesting
content.summary: Use `if`/`elif` inside the loop so different rooms behave differently, and a score variable to track progress.
content.body: Use `if`/`elif` inside your loop to make different rooms behave differently:
content.note:
You can also keep a `score` variable and update it inside the loop:

```
score = 0
for i in range(1, 6):
    score = score + 10
    print("Score:", score)
```

content.title: Plan Before You Code
content.summary: Decide the rooms, events, and ending before writing a single line.
content.body:
Before writing, answer these questions:

• How many rooms will the player visit?
• Which room numbers are special (trap, treasure, boss)?
• Does the player have HP or a score that changes?
• What does the ending message say?

Your game must use:
• At least one loop
• At least one variable
• At least one `if`/`else` (or `elif`)
• At least one `print` that uses a variable

**Not into dungeons?** The same shape works for any setting — a cookie shop where each `i` is a customer, a soccer match where each `i` is a minute, a school day where each `i` is a class period. Swap the framing, keep the structure.

editorPrompt: Build your dungeon run game (or your own variation). Collect the hero's name, loop through at least 5 rooms with different events, and end with a victory message.
starterCode:
# Loop-Powered Mini Game — Final Project
# Your game needs:
#   - hero (or character) name from input()
#   - a loop through at least 5 rooms (or scenes, customers, levels...)
#   - at least one special step (trap, treasure, surprise, boss)
#   - a score or HP variable that changes
#   - a victory message at the end

name = input("What is your hero's name? ")
score = 0

# TODO: add your loop here

print("\n" + name + " completed the dungeon! Final score:", score)
progressiveHints: Start with `for i in range(1, 6):` and just print the room number inside.
Add `if i == 3:` (or whichever room) to make that room a trap or treasure.
Add `score = score + 10` inside the safe rooms, and `score = score - 5` for traps.
Don't forget: the victory `print` is **outside** the loop (no indent), so it runs once at the end.

Full mini example (with `elif`):
name = input("Hero name? ")
score = 0
for i in range(1, 6):
    if i == 3:
        print("Room 3 — trap! -5 score")
        score = score - 5
    elif i == 5:
        print("Room 5 — boss! +20 score")
        score = score + 20
    else:
        print("Room", i, "— safe. +10 score")
        score = score + 10
print(name, "finished with score:", score)
challenge: 🚀 Dive Deeper: Add a room where the player finds a secret weapon. Print a special congratulations only if they reach that room AND their score is above `20`.
